subject: Request: scoped authentication evidence + bridge clarification
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <security@orchardhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <audit@orch-audits.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: scoped auth artifacts and bridge note

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the Type II that you uploaded earlier — that helped short-list Redwood for our 2025 procurement panel. Our external audit team (copied) is asking for a few targeted artifacts to complete our acceptance review and to finalize the bridge letter for the 2024 audit window. To keep this narrow and actionable, can you provide the following within the next two weeks?

- A short bridge letter confirming the SOC 2 Type II period covered and whether there were any critical control exceptions during the window. PDF preferred.
- MFA evidence: configuration screenshots for administrative console (showing required factors, enforcement policy), and a one-page statement on exception handling (what we should expect if someone is exempted).
- Auth logs slice: an extract of authentication events (successful login, failed login, password reset, MFA challenges) covering 2024-12-01 through 2025-02-28. We only need a sample/sliced CSV sized ~10k rows showing format/schema. Please include column names and timezone.
- Access review artifacts: a copy of the most recent quarterly access review (redaction ok) that shows reviewer, scope, and remediation actions for privileged accounts.
- Service account inventory and any documented rotation/credential expiry policy for non-human keys.

If possible, please also note retention windows for auth logs and where they are stored (cloud project/region) so we can confirm our retention expectations. We will accept sanitized artifacts — we only need evidence that controls exist and operate.

Let me know if you want us to sign an NDA or a limited evidence-sharing agreement.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Information Security Manager, Orchard Health
security@orchardhealth.com

Attachments: sample_evidence_template.xlsx (template of expected columns)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: scoped auth artifacts and bridge note

Thanks Lena — appreciate the clear scope. We're happy to provide the artifacts you listed. Quick plan and clarifying Qs:

Plan (won't all be public links; we'll provide redacted/samples via a secure share):
- Bridge letter (PDF): Compliance will draft and route for signatures — target 48 hours.
- SOC 2 PDF: we'll include the Type II report (we previously shared 2024 copy) and call out the exact covered period in the bridge letter.
- MFA screenshots + exception handling note: we'll package screenshots from the admin console and a one-page policy excerpt.
- Auth logs slice: Marcus, can you extract the 2024-12-01 -> 2025-02-28 sample (CSV). We need to confirm timezone (we keep UTC logs) and which columns to include. Lena: is your team okay with UTC timestamps and hashed user identifiers?
- Access review: Laura will attach the latest quarterly review artifact (redacted PII).
- Service account inventory and rotation policy: Marcus/Infra to produce.

Clarifying questions for scope:
1) Do you require raw session tokens or only event-level records? We typically do not export tokens; we can show session start/stop, token issuance events, and revocation records.
2) For privileged sessions, do you need keystroke/recording evidence or just privileged session logs and the review evidence?

I'll start the bridge letter draft and share a secure folder (Drive link) once attachments are ready. Marcus and Laura — can you confirm ETA for your pieces? We are targeting Thursday EOD 2025-06-12 for the first bundle.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Security (on behalf of Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Marcus here — action items and plan:
- Auth logs slice: I will extract UTC-based event-level CSV with columns: event_time_utc, event_type, principal_type (human/service), principal_id_hash, source_ip, outcome, mfa_challenge, device_fingerprint, user_agent. I will also include an additional column 'action_token_revoked' where applicable.
- Size/format constraints: we'll generate a compressed CSV and a plaintext schema file. We will not include raw tokens or raw session payloads.
- Retention: current retention is 18 months for full auth logs; 3 years for aggregated security telemetry.
- Service accounts: generating inventory where we list name, owner, last-rotation-date, rotation-policy-ref (link), and credential type. Redaction will hash IDs.

Questions for Compliance: do we need to include KMS key IDs/regions in artifacts? We can reference keystore rotations abstractly but cannot provide raw KMS keys.

ETA: I can deliver the log slice and inventory file by Thu 2025-06-12 EOD. I'll upload to the secure folder and mark files with partial hashes for verification.

Attachments: manifest_of_files.txt (planned filenames), sample_schema.txt

Marcus Lin
SRE - Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <security@orchardhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <audit@orch-audits.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: scoped auth artifacts and bridge note

Kimberly — thanks, that's helpful. We confirm the following:

- UTC timestamps are fine; hashed principal IDs acceptable as long as the same hashing scheme is applied across the sample and inventory.
- No raw session tokens required — event-level records + revocation events are sufficient.
- For privileged sessions, the auditor only needs session start/stop, actions summary, and that session recordings are archived per policy; no keystroke dumps.
- Please include a short statement on log integrity (who has write access, whether logs are WORM or append-only, and whether you use HMAC/digital signatures).

If you can surface the partial hash (first 8 chars) in filenames and provide checksums (SHA256) for all artifacts, the audit team can ingest quickly. We'll also accept the bridge letter PDF and the Type II copy.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync if anything needs to be walked through — I have availability Mon 6/16 morning PT.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Information Security Manager, Orchard Health

Attachments: acceptance_criteria_v1.pdf (short list from audit)
